A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same Brownian-bridge representation and sequence-evaluation research, despite substantial changes in title and emphasis. All pages, including appendices, equations, tables, and figures, are readable and support comparison.

before.justification: v3 reports original coherence, Human-AI discrimination, encoder-comparison, and out-of-domain experiments, with further analyses in its appendices.

after.justification: v4 reports original sequence-evaluation experiments, latent-space visualizations, backbone and loss comparisons, and runtime measurements, including retained appendix results.

M1.justification: v3's SPM uses a normalized quadratic residual; v4's BBScoreV2 uses normalized full log density, retaining determinant terms and making larger scores preferable (Equation 5). v4 also introduces an AnInfoNCE adaptation with trainable diagonal scaling and removes SPM+CLS. The SP encoder survives in Appendix A. Equation 2 additionally changes the written contrastive distance by a factor of T, without establishing whether implementation changed accordingly.

E1.justification: v4 removes the WSJ news-domain evaluation and the local discrimination task based on perturbing three-sentence windows, both present in v3. WikiSection, WikiText, global/mixed shuffling, and HC3 Human-AI discrimination remain. Losing a distinct domain and local-perturbation scenario substantially narrows coverage.

E2.justification: v4 Table 4 adds AnInfoNCE alongside the retained SP encoder, now labeled Likelihood. SPM+CLS disappears from the global coherence comparison, and SP-encoder variants disappear from the O.O.D. comparison. EntityGrid, UnifiedCoherence, BBScore, and DetectGPT remain in their corresponding core comparisons.

E3.justification: v4 adds HC3-human-answer encoder training and experiments across GPT-2, LLaMA3, and Qwen3 configurations; v3's HC3 evaluation used a WikiSection-trained encoder. The stated Wikipedia transfer direction changes from WikiSection-to-WikiText in v3 Table 5 to WikiText-to-WikiSection in v4 Table 2, despite identical corresponding numbers. This establishes a reported protocol revision, without confirming a rerun.

E4.justification: v4 adds raw-versus-encoded PCA analysis, backbone sensitivity studies, an AnInfoNCE loss ablation, and runtime scaling analysis. v3's covariance/trajectory comparisons and score-versus-length stability plots are removed. The epsilon tuning and Human-AI covariance/DetectGPT perturbation comparisons remain in reorganized appendices.

E5.justification: v4 Figure 4 newly reports an ordinary-least-squares fit for runtime scaling, with slope 1.57. Neither version reports repeated-run accuracy uncertainty, seed counts, confidence intervals, or formal significance tests.

E6.justification: WikiSection result rows are replaced: at block size 1, v3 SPM reports 95.06% global and 90.32% mixed accuracy, while v4 GPT2-based BBScoreV2 reports 99.03% and 94.78%. Mixed accuracy at block size 10 changes from 77.89% to 70.83%. These accompany revised formulations. New backbone, ablation, PCA, and timing results appear; local/WSJ results disappear. The Human-AI tables retain their numerical values.

T1.justification: The likelihood and covariance-MLE propositions and proofs are retained, moving to v4 Appendix C. However, v3's chi-square normalization derivation and the resulting positivity and concentration-around-one properties are removed when the score becomes log density divided by d(T-1). This substantially revises the central metric's mathematical definition and calibration.

C1.justification: v3 presents the SP encoder's superiority over contrastive learning and its O.O.D. robustness as central contributions. v4's abstract, introduction, and conclusion replace that contribution with the claim that an MLP transforms clustered language-model embeddings into temporally ordered representations. Likelihood-based evaluation and Human-AI detection remain central claims.

C2.justification: v3 attributes SP-encoder advantages to learning structural correlations. v4 Section 5.4 instead interprets its ablations as showing that the MLP primarily reconstructs temporal information, with correlations originating in raw embeddings or domain statistics. v4 adds backbone-related tradeoff explanations and specific limitations concerning missing human-preference validation and limited detection benchmarking; v3's local-perturbation weakness discussion disappears.

D1.justification: v4 newly explains HC3 question-answer concatenation, answer-only inputs, and label construction, and reports backbone hidden dimensions of 768 versus 2048. The SPM+CLS feature-window and classifier-architecture details are removed. SP-encoder hardware, optimizers, learning rates, epochs, regularization settings, and code/data access information are retained.

R1.justification: v3 positions its SP encoder as overcoming deficiencies in Wang et al.'s contrastive encoder; v4 adopts that encoder centrally and withdraws the novel-encoder superiority positioning. Geshkovski et al. (2023) and Rusak et al. (2024) support the new clustering narrative and anisotropic ablation, while the WSJ reference is removed. The relationship to prior encoder research changes substantially.

P1.justification: The title, abstract, introduction, research questions, and conclusion are extensively rewritten around temporal alignment. Related work moves before the method, dataset descriptions move into Appendix D, and SP-encoder material is consolidated in Appendix A. The narrative is substantially reorganized beyond renaming SPM.

P2.justification: v4 adopts a two-column layout, redraws Figure 1, groups key equations in a boxed panel, and merges global/mixed-shuffle results into Table 1. New PCA, backbone, and runtime figures replace earlier covariance, trajectory, moving-window, and length-stability displays. These are substantial visual and table-structure changes.

improvement.justification: v4 adds useful representation, backbone, loss, and runtime analyses and explicit limitations. However, its revised score retains a length-dependent determinant term while dropping v3's calibration argument, despite retaining length-invariance claims. Identical O.O.D. numbers also receive reversed training/test descriptions (v3 Table 5; v4 Table 2). The PDFs do not resolve how revised definitions and settings relate to retained results, preventing a reliable assessment of whether the added analyses outweigh these scientific consistency problems.
